lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Good morning! What would you like?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: I would like a sandwich and a coffee, please.

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Would you like milk in your coffee?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Yes, please. And a glass of water.

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Anything else?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: No, thank you. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: That is eight dollars.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Here you are.

lines.speaker: Server
lines.text: Thank you. Have a nice day!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hi, Leo. It's Mia. Do you have the math homework?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yes. We have to do page twelve, exercises one and two.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Thanks. Do you want to study together?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Sure. Let's meet at the library at five.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: OK. See you at five. Bye!

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Bye!

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Hi, Nina! How was the beach?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: It was great! The weather was sunny and warm.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: What did you do there?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: I swam in the sea and found a small shell.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Nice! Did you take photos?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Yes, I did. I can show you on Monday.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Great. What time did you go home?

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: We went home at five o'clock.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hi, Alex. Are you free next weekend?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: No, I'm not. I'm going to visit my grandparents.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Oh, nice. What are you going to do there?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: I'm going to work in the garden and walk to the lake.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: When are you going to come home?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: On Sunday evening. Do you want to play football on Monday?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Sure! Let's meet at the park at four.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Great. See you on Monday!

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Good afternoon. Welcome to the Park Hotel.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Hello. I have a reservation for two people. My name is Sofia Ramos.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Let me check. Yes, a room for two nights. Is that correct?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Yes, that's right. Is breakfast included?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes, breakfast is from seven to ten in the café on the first floor.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Great. What time is check-out?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Check-out is at eleven. Here are your keys. Your room is on the fifth floor.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Good morning, Leo. What seems to be the problem?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I have a headache and a sore throat. I feel very tired.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: How long have you felt like this?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Since Sunday evening. I also have a cough.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Do you have a temperature?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yes, I think so.

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: You have a bad cold. Stay home for two days and drink a lot of water.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Should I take any medicine?

lines.speaker: Doctor
lines.text: Yes, take this for your headache. And no football this week.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: OK. Thank you, Doctor.

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Good morning. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Hello. I ordered a pair of running shoes last week, but I received the wrong size.

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: I'm sorry about that. What is your order number?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: It's four seven two nine.

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Thank you. I see the order: blue shoes, size thirty-eight. What did you receive?

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Black shoes, size thirty-six.

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: We will send the correct shoes today. The return is free. Please use the same box.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Thank you. How long will the delivery take?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Two or three days.

lines.speaker: Emma
lines.text: Great. Thank you for your help.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.text: Hello, Mr. Brown speaking.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Hello. This is Anna Miller. We moved into apartment three B last week.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.text: Yes, of course. Is everything OK?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Almost. The kitchen window does not close, and the hot water is not working.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.text: I'm sorry about that. I can send a repair person tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Thank you. What time will he come?

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.text: Between nine and eleven. Will someone be at home?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Yes, I will be at home.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.text: Good. I will call you when he is on his way.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: Hello? Mia, are you on the train?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Not yet. The train is late. It will leave at six fifteen.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: Oh no. What about the show?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: We have tickets for eight o'clock. If we arrive at seven thirty, we can still go.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: I hope so. Are you OK?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Yes, we are fine. We are drinking coffee and waiting.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: Call me when you arrive in London.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I will. Bye, Mom.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Come in, Maya. How was your first week?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: It was busy, but I enjoyed it. I have learned a lot.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: What was the most difficult part?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: The software. I made a mistake in the report on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: I saw that. You told me immediately, and that was the right thing to do.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I was worried, but my colleagues helped me.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Good. Next week, I would like you to lead the short meeting on Monday.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Me? I have never led a meeting before.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: You do not need to be perfect. Prepare three questions and listen to the team.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: OK. I will prepare on Friday.

lines.speaker: Mr. Chen
lines.text: Good. And Maya, ask for help when you need it. That is part of the job.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Thank you. I will.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.text: Hi, Lena! How is life in the city?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: It is very different from our town. I am still getting used to it.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.text: What do you miss most?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I miss the quiet mornings and my old friends. The city is noisy, but there are more things to do.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.text: How is your new job?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: It is interesting. I have met many people, and I have learned to use the subway.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.text: Do you like your apartment?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Yes, it is smaller than our old house, but it is close to a park.

lines.speaker: Jenny
lines.text: I am glad. Come and visit us when you can.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I will. I am going to come back next month.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Welcome to the podcast. Today we are talking about plastic.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Thank you. I am happy to be here.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: You tried to live without plastic for a month. Was it difficult?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Yes, especially at the beginning. Plastic is everywhere.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What was the hardest thing to avoid?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Food packaging. It is almost impossible to buy some products without plastic.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What did you learn?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: I learned that small changes matter. If we all use a reusable bag, we will reduce waste.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What would you say to people who think one person cannot make a difference?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: I would say: start with one product. Then try another. Change is easier when it is small.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Thank you. That is a good place to stop.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Welcome. Today we are talking about rumors and social media.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: Thank you. It is a very important topic.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: A story about a local school spread last week. What happened?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: Someone posted that the school was going to close. It was not true.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: How did you check it?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: I called the school, the city office, and the parents' group.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What did you find?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: The post was written by a person who did not work at the school.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What should people do before sharing a story?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: Ask three questions: Who wrote it? What is the evidence? Who else reports it?

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Thank you. That is good advice.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: OK, let's start. The festival is in three weeks. What do we need to finish?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The poster. We have the design, but we have not printed it yet.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: Can you print it this week?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yes, I can. I will ask the art teacher for help.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: We also need more tables. The shop said they can lend us ten.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: Great. Who will collect them?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I will. I can take my father's car on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: Good. What about the music?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: The music teacher is away. Maybe we can ask the older students to play.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: Good idea. I will ask them tomorrow. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: We need to decide what to do if it rains.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: We will move everything into the hall. OK, let's meet again on Friday.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Today we are discussing the cost of university. Does a degree still justify the price?

lines.speaker: Student A
lines.text: I think it does, but only for some careers. Medicine or law requires a degree.

lines.speaker: Student B
lines.text: But many graduates work in jobs that do not require a degree. They still have debt.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: What does the evidence say?

lines.speaker: Student A
lines.text: Graduates earn more on average, but the gap is smaller in some fields.

lines.speaker: Student B
lines.text: And online courses and apprenticeships are cheaper. They may be better for practical skills.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: So the value depends on the field and the person?

lines.speaker: Student A
lines.text: Yes. A degree is an investment, but not a guarantee.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: What about the social side? University is also about meeting people and learning to think.

lines.speaker: Student B
lines.text: That is true, but students can get that in other ways too.

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Good point. For next week, find one piece of data on graduate earnings and one on alternative routes.

lines.speaker: Student A
lines.text: Should we focus on the US or compare countries?

lines.speaker: Professor
lines.text: Compare at least two countries. That will make your argument stronger.

lines.speaker: Student B
lines.text: OK. See you next week.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Thank you for coming. We are thinking about a four-day week trial.

lines.speaker: Employee A
lines.text: How would the work be organized? We already have too many meetings.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: We would cut meetings by half and protect two hours of quiet work each day.

lines.speaker: Employee B
lines.text: Would we work longer days from Monday to Thursday?

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Yes, eight and a half hours instead of eight. Friday would be free.

lines.speaker: Employee A
lines.text: I like the idea, but some clients need support on Friday.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: We would keep a small Friday team and rotate it.

lines.speaker: Employee B
lines.text: What about pay? Would it stay the same?

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Yes. The trial would last three months, and pay would not change.

lines.speaker: Employee A
lines.text: How will we measure success?

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: We will track output, sick days, and how people feel. If output falls, we will change the plan.

lines.speaker: Employee B
lines.text: That sounds fair. I would join the trial.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Good. I will send the details on Monday.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Today we are talking about rewilding cities. What does that mean?

lines.speaker: Ecologist
lines.text: It means giving nature more space in urban areas: green roofs, wild gardens, and corridors for animals.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Why is it important?

lines.speaker: Ecologist
lines.text: Cities are getting hotter. Trees and plants cool the air and absorb rainwater. They also support insects and birds.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Is it expensive?

lines.speaker: Ecologist
lines.text: It can be, but not always. A wild garden is cheaper than a parking lot. The challenge is maintenance and public support.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Some people worry about safety or allergies. What do you say?

lines.speaker: Ecologist
lines.text: Those concerns are real. A good plan includes paths, clear information, and areas for different uses.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What would you do first in a city?

lines.speaker: Ecologist
lines.text: Start with small spaces: school grounds, rooftops, and empty corners. If people see the results, they will support bigger projects.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: So rewilding is as much about people as about nature?

lines.speaker: Ecologist
lines.text: Exactly. If the community is involved, the project lasts.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Welcome. Today: can we trust the news?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: We can trust good journalism, but we need to check who paid for the story.

lines.speaker: Platform Rep
lines.text: Platforms give people more sources than ever. That is a positive change.

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: More sources is not the same as more understanding. Algorithms reward attention.

lines.speaker: Platform Rep
lines.text: We label political ads and explain why we show content.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What should readers do?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: Compare two sources, check the date, and look for evidence.

lines.speaker: Platform Rep
lines.text: And report false information. We can reduce its reach.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Is regulation the answer?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: Transparency helps. But regulation must protect independent journalism too.

lines.speaker: Platform Rep
lines.text: We support clear rules if they are the same for everyone.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What is the biggest risk?

lines.speaker: Journalist
lines.text: That people stop trusting everything, including reliable reporting.

lines.speaker: Platform Rep
lines.text: Or that they trust only the voices that make them angry.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Thank you both.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Are algorithms making hiring fairer or less fair?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Both are possible. It depends on the data and the goal.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What is the biggest risk?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: A model learns from past decisions. If the past was unfair, the model can repeat it.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: How can companies reduce the risk?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Audit the model, test different groups, and keep human review.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What about performance monitoring?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: It can help, but workers need to know what is measured and why.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Should governments regulate?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Yes, but rules should be clear and consistent. Companies need to know what is expected.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: What should workers do?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Ask questions. If a decision is automated, ask for an explanation and a human review.

lines.speaker: Host
lines.text: Thank you. That is a useful place to end.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: Let's review the survey results. What did students ask for most?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Later library hours. Almost sixty percent mentioned it.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And more vegetarian food. The café has very few options.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: What about the bike shelter?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: It was popular, but the cost is higher than we thought.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The garden is cheaper. We could start with a small pilot.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: We need to present three options and a recommendation.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I can prepare the cost table.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I will write the section on student well-being.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: Good. What about the presentation?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: We have ten minutes and five slides.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I can design the slides, but someone else should speak.

lines.speaker: Chair
lines.text: I will speak. We need to rehearse on Thursday.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Agreed. Let's meet at four.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Come in, Maya. You wanted to talk about your project.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes. I am studying how people use the new public space near the station.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: That is a good topic. What is your research question?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I want to know if the space changed how often people talk to their neighbors.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Interesting. How will you collect data?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I plan to interview twenty residents and count how many people use the space at different times.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Good. You should also observe the space on a weekend. The pattern may be different.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I will. When should I send you the first draft?

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: By Friday, please. Then we can meet on March 12.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: How long should the report be?

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: About five pages, not more. Focus on the evidence, not on background.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Should I include photos?

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: One or two, if they help. But do not use photos of people without permission.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Understood. I will send the questions to you before I start the interviews.

lines.speaker: Professor Grant
lines.text: Perfect. And Maya, remember to keep a research diary. It will help you explain your choices later.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I will. Thank you, Professor Grant.
